title: (a + b)² — Algebraic Identity Formula & Derivation
answer: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² (or a² + b² + 2ab). It is the fundamental algebraic identity for the square of a binomial sum. Expanding step-by-step: (a + b)(a + b) = a(a + b) + b(a + b) = a² + ab + ba + b² = a² + 2ab + b².
highlights: Formula: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²
Expansion: (a + b)(a + b) = a² + 2ab + b²
Geometric Meaning: The area of a square with side length (a + b)
Related Identity: (a - b)² = a² - 2ab + b²

title: (a - b)² — Algebraic Identity Formula & Derivation
answer: (a - b)² = a² - 2ab + b² (or a² + b² - 2ab). It is the standard algebraic identity for the square of a binomial difference. Expanding step-by-step: (a - b)(a - b) = a(a - b) - b(a - b) = a² - ab - ba + b² = a² - 2ab + b².
highlights: Formula: (a - b)² = a² - 2ab + b²
Expansion: (a - b)(a - b) = a² - 2ab + b²
Related Identity: a² - b² = (a + b)(a - b)

title: a² - b² (Difference of Two Squares)
answer: a² - b² = (a + b)(a - b). This fundamental algebraic identity states that the difference of two squares equals the product of their sum and their difference.
highlights: Formula: a² - b² = (a + b)(a - b)
Use Case: Factoring polynomials, mental calculation, calculus integration

title: (a + b)³ — Algebraic Cube Identity
answer: (a + b)³ = a³ + 3a²b + 3ab² + b³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b). It represents the expansion of a binomial cubed and geometrically corresponds to the volume of a cube with side (a + b).
highlights: Standard Form: (a + b)³ = a³ + 3a²b + 3ab² + b³
Factored Form: (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b)
Related Formula: (a - b)³ = a³ - 3a²b + 3ab² - b³ = a³ - b³ - 3ab(a - b)

title: (a - b)³ — Algebraic Difference Cube Identity
answer: (a - b)³ = a³ - 3a²b + 3ab² - b³ = a³ - b³ - 3ab(a - b). It is the formula for the cube of a difference of two terms.
highlights: Standard Form: (a - b)³ = a³ - 3a²b + 3ab² - b³
Factored Form: (a - b)³ = a³ - b³ - 3ab(a - b)
Sign Rule: Signs alternate +, -, +, -

title: a³ + b³ (Sum of Two Cubes)
answer: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² - ab + b²). This identity factorizes the sum of two cubed terms into a linear binomial and a quadratic trinomial.
highlights: Formula: a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² - ab + b²)
Alternative Form: a³ + b³ = (a + b)³ - 3ab(a + b)
Related Identity: a³ - b³ = (a - b)(a² + ab + b²)

title: a³ - b³ (Difference of Two Cubes)
answer: a³ - b³ = (a - b)(a² + ab + b²). This identity factorizes the difference of two cubed terms.
highlights: Formula: a³ - b³ = (a - b)(a² + ab + b²)
Alternative Form: a³ - b³ = (a - b)³ + 3ab(a - b)
Sign Tip: The first factor (a - b) has a minus sign, while the second factor has all positive terms (a² + ab + b²)

title: (a + b + c)² — Trinomial Square Identity
answer: (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca) = a² + b² + c² + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca. It expands the square of a sum of three terms.
highlights: Formula: (a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2ab + 2bc + 2ca
Factorized Group: a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca)
Use Case: Three-dimensional geometry and coordinate distance derivations

title: Pythagorean Theorem (a² + b² = c²)
answer: In any right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse (c) is equal to the sum of the squares of the other two sides (a and b): a² + b² = c².
highlights: Formula: a² + b² = c² (or c = √(a² + b²))
Applications: Euclidean geometry, 2D/3D distance formula, vector magnitude, navigation

title: Quadratic Formula (Roots of ax² + bx + c = 0)
answer: For any quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0 (where a ≠ 0), the roots are given by x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a).
highlights: Formula: x = [-b ± √(b² - 4ac)] / (2a)
Discriminant (D = b² - 4ac): D > 0 (2 distinct real roots), D = 0 (1 repeated real root), D < 0 (2 complex conjugate roots)
Discovered By: Ancient Indian mathematician Sridhara (Sridharacharya)

title: Circle Formulas — Area & Circumference
answer: The area of a circle with radius r is A = πr² (or πd²/4). The circumference (perimeter) of a circle is C = 2πr (or πd).
highlights: Area Formula: A = πr² (where r is radius, d = 2r is diameter)
Circumference Formula: C = 2πr = πd
Arc Length: L = (θ / 360°) × 2πr (for angle θ in degrees)
Sector Area: A_sector = (θ / 360°) × πr²

title: Sphere — Volume & Surface Area Formulas
answer: The volume of a sphere of radius r is V = (4/3)πr³. The total surface area of a sphere is SA = 4πr².
highlights: Volume Formula: V = (4/3)πr³
Surface Area Formula: SA = 4πr²
Hemisphere Volume: V_hemi = (2/3)πr³
Hemisphere Total Surface Area: TSA = 3πr² (Curved Surface Area = 2πr²)

title: Cylinder — Volume & Surface Area Formulas
answer: The volume of a right circular cylinder of radius r and height h is V = πr²h. Its curved surface area is CSA = 2πrh and total surface area is TSA = 2πr(r + h).
highlights: Volume: V = πr²h
Curved Surface Area (CSA): 2πrh
Total Surface Area (TSA): 2πr(r + h) = 2πrh + 2πr²
Cross-sectional Base Area: πr²

title: Cone — Volume & Surface Area Formulas
answer: The volume of a right circular cone of radius r and vertical height h is V = (1/3)πr²h. Its curved surface area is CSA = πrl where slant height l = √(r² + h²), and total surface area is TSA = πr(r + l).
highlights: Volume: V = (1/3)πr²h (exactly one-third of a cylinder with same base and height)
Slant Height: l = √(r² + h²)
Curved Surface Area (CSA): πrl
Total Surface Area (TSA): πr(r + l) = πrl + πr²

title: Euler's Formula & Identity (e^(iπ) + 1 = 0)
answer: Euler's formula in complex analysis states that e^(ix) = cos(x) + i sin(x). When x = π, it yields Euler's identity: e^(iπ) + 1 = 0, widely hailed as the most beautiful equation in mathematics.
highlights: Euler's Formula: e^(ix) = cos(x) + i sin(x)
Euler's Identity: e^(iπ) + 1 = 0 (unites five fundamental constants: 0, 1, e, i, π)
Polyhedral Formula: V - E + F = 2 (Vertices - Edges + Faces = 2 for convex polyhedra)

title: Fundamental Trigonometric Pythagorean Identities
answer: The primary Pythagorean trigonometric identities are: 1) sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1; 2) 1 + tan²(θ) = sec²(θ); 3) 1 + cot²(θ) = csc²(θ).
highlights: Primary Identity: sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1
Tangent-Secant: 1 + tan²(θ) = sec²(θ)  [or sec²(θ) - tan²(θ) = 1]
Cotangent-Cosecant: 1 + cot²(θ) = csc²(θ)  [or csc²(θ) - cot²(θ) = 1]
Basic Ratios: tan(θ) = sin(θ)/cos(θ), cot(θ) = cos(θ)/sin(θ), sec(θ) = 1/cos(θ), csc(θ) = 1/sin(θ)

title: Trigonometric Compound Angle Addition & Subtraction Formulas
answer: The sum and difference identities in trigonometry are: sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B; cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B; tan(A ± B) = (tan A ± tan B) / (1 ∓ tan A tan B).
highlights: Sine Sum: sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B
Sine Difference: sin(A - B) = sin A cos B - cos A sin B
Cosine Sum: cos(A + B) = cos A cos B - sin A sin B (sign flips!)
Cosine Difference: cos(A - B) = cos A cos B + sin A sin B
Tangent Sum: tan(A + B) = (tan A + tan B) / (1 - tan A tan B)

title: Double Angle Trigonometric Formulas (sin 2x, cos 2x, tan 2x)
answer: The double angle formulas are: sin(2x) = 2 sin(x) cos(x); cos(2x) = cos²(x) - sin²(x) = 2cos²(x) - 1 = 1 - 2sin²(x); tan(2x) = 2tan(x) / (1 - tan²(x)).
highlights: Sine Double Angle: sin(2x) = 2 sin(x) cos(x) = 2tan(x) / (1 + tan²(x))
Cosine Double Angle: cos(2x) = cos²(x) - sin²(x) = 2cos²(x) - 1 = 1 - 2sin²(x) = (1 - tan²(x))/(1 + tan²(x))
Tangent Double Angle: tan(2x) = 2tan(x) / (1 - tan²(x))

title: Heron's Formula — Area of a Triangle with Three Known Sides
answer: Heron's formula gives the area of a triangle with side lengths a, b, c as Area = √(s(s - a)(s - b)(s - c)), where s = (a + b + c) / 2 is the semi-perimeter.
highlights: Formula: Area = √(s(s - a)(s - b)(s - c))
Semi-perimeter: s = (a + b + c) / 2
Discovered By: Hero of Alexandria (c. 60 CE)

title: Calculus Differentiation Rules & Derivatives Cheat Sheet
answer: The fundamental derivative rules are: Power Rule: d/dx(xⁿ) = n·xⁿ⁻¹; Product Rule: (uv)' = u'v + uv'; Quotient Rule: (u/v)' = (u'v - uv')/v²; Chain Rule: d/dx[f(g(x))] = f'(g(x))·g'(x).
highlights: Power Rule: d/dx(xⁿ) = n·xⁿ⁻¹
Product Rule: d/dx[u·v] = u·(dv/dx) + v·(du/dx)
Quotient Rule: d/dx[u/v] = (v·du/dx - u·dv/dx) / v²
Trig Derivatives: d/dx(sin x) = cos x, d/dx(cos x) = -sin x, d/dx(tan x) = sec² x
Exponential: d/dx(eˣ) = eˣ, d/dx(ln x) = 1/x

title: Calculus Integration Formulas & Fundamental Rules
answer: The basic integration rules are: Power Rule: ∫ xⁿ dx = (xⁿ⁺¹)/(n + 1) + C (for n ≠ -1); ∫ (1/x) dx = ln|x| + C; ∫ eˣ dx = eˣ + C; Integration by Parts: ∫ u dv = uv - ∫ v du.
highlights: Power Rule: ∫ xⁿ dx = (xⁿ⁺¹)/(n + 1) + C (n ≠ -1)
Logarithmic: ∫ (1/x) dx = ln|x| + C
Exponential: ∫ eˣ dx = eˣ + C
Integration by Parts: ∫ u dv = uv - ∫ v du (based on product rule of differentiation)
Trigonometric Integrals: ∫ sin x dx = -cos x + C, ∫ cos x dx = sin x + C, ∫ sec²x dx = tan x + C

title: Logarithm Rules & Properties Reference
answer: The core logarithm laws are: Product: log_b(xy) = log_b(x) + log_b(y); Quotient: log_b(x/y) = log_b(x) - log_b(y); Power: log_b(xᵏ) = k·log_b(x); Change of Base: log_b(x) = ln(x) / ln(b) = log_c(x) / log_c(b).
highlights: Product Rule: log(xy) = log(x) + log(y)
Quotient Rule: log(x/y) = log(x) - log(y)
Power Rule: log(xᵏ) = k·log(x)
Special Values: log_b(1) = 0, log_b(b) = 1, log_b(bᵏ) = k
Change of Base: log_a(b) = log_c(b) / log_c(a)

title: Arithmetic Progression (AP) & Geometric Progression (GP) Formulas
answer: For Arithmetic Progression (AP): nth term a_n = a + (n - 1)d, Sum S_n = (n/2)[2a + (n - 1)d] = (n/2)(first + last). For Geometric Progression (GP): nth term a_n = a·rⁿ⁻¹, Sum S_n = a(rⁿ - 1)/(r - 1) (for r ≠ 1), Infinite sum S_∞ = a/(1 - r) for |r| < 1.
highlights: AP nth Term: a_n = a + (n - 1)d (where a = 1st term, d = common difference)
GP nth Term: a_n = a·rⁿ⁻¹ (where r = common ratio)
GP Sum: S_n = a(1 - rⁿ)/(1 - r) for r < 1; Infinite GP Sum = a/(1 - r) (|r| < 1)
